_comment: Selective per-tool policy, informed by the spike's measured per-tool savings (gh records +16-30%, runecho +25-29%, kb +2.6%, single objects +0%). First matching rule wins; unmatched tools use defaults. tiers subset of [minify, tabularize, dictionary]; [] = passthrough. Lossless by default. Per-field lossy is opt-in: 'truncate' executes (gated by an acceptable-loss check); 'summarize'/'drop-to-retrieve' are parsed but deferred (warned). A field marked {critical:true} is never made lossy.
_comment_server_scope: A SERVER-scoped rule below ('runecho.*', 'codegraph.*') only matches when the proxy knows which server it is fronting: `proxy --server-name runecho` (install-mcp bakes this in from your MCP config; --config uses each peer's name). Without it, only the tool's own name is matched — which is why 'kb.*' works unaided (kb names its tools kb.read.*) while 'runecho.*' would silently miss runecho's plainly-named 'structure' tool and fall through to defaults. See #83.

policies._comment: secret-broker, rule 1 of 2 — the ONE tool measured safe AND worth compressing: list_credentials returns ~70 uniform records (metadata only, never values — verified by a live leak check) and compresses 45.5% (3521->1918 cl100k), the best in the fleet. 'capture': false still applies: compress it, never persist it. Requires proxy --server-name secret-broker, since the tools are named secret.* and would not otherwise match a secret-broker.* glob (#83).

secret-broker, rule 2 of 2 — DEFAULT-DENY for the crown-jewel server. Everything else gets tiers:[] (no compression, and critically no in-memory diff base) + capture:false (never on disk, neither corpus nor debug-log, #85). This is deliberately fail-SAFE rather than specific-deny: reveal_credential returns a plaintext value by design and inject_env returns subprocess stdout that may echo one, but more importantly a FUTURE secret-broker tool that returns a value inherits zero retention automatically instead of silently getting compressed. The payload-free ledger still counts every tool here, so opting one in later is a measurement, not a guess. require_server_name:true makes the proxy refuse to start without --server-name secret-broker, rather than silently letting this rule go unreachable (its glob needs the qualified candidate, same reason as rule 1's comment) and falling through to the permissive default (#243).
Verbose record/symbol APIs — full Tier-0/0.5 pays (16-30%).

result[].body._note: keep first 500 chars + a loss marker

policies._comment: codegraph: search/query JSON measured +33%. explore/node return markdown+source (non-JSON), which the lossless codec cannot fold — measured 0.0% saved on 60 real payloads, of which 89.2% of the tokens were fenced code blocks. '$text.code_blocks' is the OPT-IN Tier-1 lossy answer: each fenced block over 'min' chars leaves the wire as a retrieve handle while the exploration summary and blast-radius prose stay resident. Measured 87.0% fewer tokens on that same corpus, byte-exact restore verified on every payload. LOSSY — the model must call terse.retrieve to read the source back; delete this field to stay 100% lossless.

Re-measured post-#116 join on 1,657 captured payloads: dictionary now has a multi-block record array to fold into, not the single-block case the original +2.6%-total call was made on. Fleet: 7.5% -> 8.0% (+0.6pp). Per-tool: kb.read.node_history 8.6% -> 18.5%, lodestone_search 10.9% -> 44.0%, kb.read.changelog 37.4% -> 44.7% (#144).
Status/single-object endpoints measured +0% — skip entirely to avoid transform cost.
